info.name: detector
info.description:
Open-vocabulary object detection — POST an image and a list of free-text labels, get boxes back in the image's ORIGINAL pixel coordinates. No fixed class list and no fine-tuning: "swimming pool", "roof vent" and "solar panel" work exactly as well as "car" does.

Called through the LiteLLM pass-through registered in ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml (`pass_through_endpoints` → `/v1/detector` → `http://detector:8000`, `include_subpath: true`, methods GET/POST, `forward_headers: true`). Every request is authenticated with a Bearer token from a LiteLLM virtual key. Set the collection variables `litellm` (e.g. http://localhost:4001) and `virtual master key` (an sk-… key issued from the LiteLLM Admin UI → Virtual Keys) — every request inherits them via collection-level auth. See ai/detector/DETECTOR.md for the operator guide and ai/litellm/LITELLM.md for issuing virtual keys.

Direct base URL (bypassing LiteLLM): http://detector:8000 inside the ai_shared network, or http://<host>:${PORT_DETECTOR} (default 8021), which the ai/edge HAProxy publishes for clients in EDGE_ALLOWED_CIDRS and answers with 503 + Retry-After while the detector is recreated or still loading its model. There is NO auth on the service itself — the pass-through is what does the bearer check, so do not publish that port on an untrusted network.

Synchronous, not a job queue: /detect blocks until the model answers (a few hundred ms on the GPU, a few seconds on the DETECTOR_DEVICE=cpu fallback) and returns the boxes inline. One inference runs at a time, so concurrent callers queue.

Coordinates: every `box` is `[x1, y1, x2, y2]`, top-left origin, in the ORIGINAL pixels of the image you sent (after EXIF transpose), clipped to the image. The service's internal resize to DETECTOR_MAX_IMAGE_SIDE and OWLv2's square padding are both undone before the response — see DETECTOR.md § Coordinates.

Scores are NOT calibrated probabilities. 0.65 is a confident detection for OWLv2; the same number on another label in another photo means something else. Treat `threshold` as a knob to turn, not a percentage — 0.2–0.3 is the normal working range.

**Error bodies.** Each endpoint's `#### Schemas` section -- at the end of its first request's description, generated from `detector.schemas.json` by `scripts/api_schemas.py render` -- documents its request body, its success response and every error status whose body is more than FastAPI's `{"detail": "<message>"}`. Any other error answers that `{"detail": "<message>"}`; a request that fails FastAPI's own validation answers 422 `{"detail": [{"type", "loc", "msg", "input", ...}]}`, one entry per problem. A request sent through LiteLLM (`{{litellm}}`) can also be refused by LiteLLM itself before it reaches the service -- 401 / 403 for a missing or unauthorised key -- with LiteLLM's `{"error": {"message", "type", "param", "code"}}`.

variable.description: LiteLLM base URL. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); on ai_shared it's http://litellm:4000; behind cloudflared it's https://your-litellm-host.

LiteLLM virtual key (Admin UI → Virtual Keys, or /key/generate API). The pass-through runs with `auth: true`, so a non-admin virtual key needs `/v1/detector` in its (or its team's) `metadata.allowed_passthrough_routes` — set under `metadata`, by a proxy admin, because the top-level field is Enterprise-only; the master key works without it. Otherwise 403. See ai/litellm/LITELLM.md § Pass-through auth. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}` by the collection-level auth, then forwarded to the detector by LiteLLM because the pass-through has `forward_headers: true`.

A PUBLIC http(s) image URL for the JSON-with-URL request. It is SSRF-checked before the fetch (common.net.validate_url): anything resolving to an RFC1918, loopback, or link-local address is a 400, so a LAN or container-name URL will NOT work here on purpose.

request.description:
Liveness plus the one thing that actually matters: is the model resident?

**Returns 200** `{"status": "ok", "model", "family", "device", "configured_device", "loaded": true, "error": null, "default_threshold", "max_image_side", "max_labels"}`.

**Returns 503** with `"status": "degraded"`, `"loaded": false` and the loader's error in `error` after a failed model load (a bad DETECTOR_MODEL, a Grounding DINO id, no disk) — permanently, until a recreate. It never answers during the first-start load: the weights load in the lifespan, before uvicorn accepts a connection, so a request then is refused (the ai/edge front answers its own 503 + Retry-After). That is deliberate: a container that is up with a failed model load is not healthy, and the Docker healthcheck should fail it rather than route traffic to a service that can only answer 503.

`device` is what is actually in use and is not always `configured_device` — `cuda` on a host where torch sees no GPU falls back to `cpu` with a warning rather than refusing to start. See DETECTOR.md § CPU fallback.

#### Schemas

Response `200` (`application/json`) — the weights are loaded:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "status",
    "model",
    "family",
    "device",
    "configured_device",
    "loaded",
    "error",
    "default_threshold",
    "max_image_side",
    "max_labels"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "status": {"const": "ok"},
    "model": {"type": "string", "description": "DETECTOR_MODEL"},
    "family": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The implementation family the model id resolved to"
    },
    "device": {"enum": ["cuda", "cpu"], "description": "What is actually in use"},
    "configured_device": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "DETECTOR_DEVICE as configured; `device` falls back to `cpu` when torch sees no GPU"
    },
    "loaded": {"const": true},
    "error": {"type": "null"},
    "default_threshold": {"type": "number", "description": "DETECTOR_DEFAULT_THRESHOLD"},
    "max_image_side": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 64, "description": "DETECTOR_MAX_IMAGE_SIDE"},
    "max_labels": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "description": "DETECTOR_MAX_LABELS"}
  }
}
```

Response `503` (`application/json`) — the weights are not resident, which only follows a failed model load (a bad DETECTOR_MODEL, a Grounding DINO id, no disk): the lifespan loads the weights before uvicorn accepts a connection, so during the first-start load there is no answer at all (the edge answers its own 503 + Retry-After):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "status",
    "model",
    "family",
    "device",
    "configured_device",
    "loaded",
    "error",
    "default_threshold",
    "max_image_side",
    "max_labels"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "status": {"const": "degraded"},
    "model": {"type": "string", "description": "DETECTOR_MODEL"},
    "family": {"type": "null"},
    "device": {"enum": ["cuda", "cpu"], "description": "What is actually in use"},
    "configured_device": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "DETECTOR_DEVICE as configured; `device` falls back to `cpu` when torch sees no GPU"
    },
    "loaded": {"const": false},
    "error": {"type": "string", "description": "The loader's error, `<ExceptionType>: <message>`"},
    "default_threshold": {"type": "number", "description": "DETECTOR_DEFAULT_THRESHOLD"},
    "max_image_side": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 64, "description": "DETECTOR_MAX_IMAGE_SIDE"},
    "max_labels": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "description": "DETECTOR_MAX_LABELS"}
  }
}
```

formdata.description: Repo fixture: unit-tests/classifier/Neighborhood.jpeg — a 7770×1999 street panorama. Re-select the file in Postman if your working directory differs. Any JPEG / PNG / HEIC / HEIF / AVIF works (or anything else Pillow opens) — a phone photo is turned upright once, from its EXIF tag or its HEIF container's rotation, and the boxes are in that upright frame; images below 32 px on a side are refused with a 400.

A JSON array, a comma list (`tree, house`), or one bare name — all three are accepted, because a multipart form carries strings and an n8n node or a curl user will produce all of them. Duplicates collapse; order and spelling are preserved exactly, because the label is how you match a box back to your own criterion. Capped at DETECTOR_MAX_LABELS (32).
Confidence floor 0–1. Omit for DETECTOR_DEFAULT_THRESHOLD (0.25). 0.2 is a good starting point on real photos.
Keep at most this many boxes per label, highest score first. Omit to keep every box above the threshold.

item.name: POST /detect — JSON with a base64 image

request.description:
The same request as a JSON body — what another service sends. This is the shape ai/classifier/detector/client.py uses: it base64s the ≤1000-px working page image and posts one call per page carrying every label for that page.

The `data` value shipped here is a 1×1 PNG placeholder so the request is runnable as-is; it will come back with a **400** ("Image too small") because images below 32 px on a side are refused — below that the model's answers are noise. Paste a real base64 image to get boxes. A `data:image/png;base64,…` prefix is tolerated.

`image.type` is `base64` or `url`. For `url` see the next request.

**Returns** the same body as the multipart spelling. **Errors:** 400 (invalid base64, undecodable or too-small image), 503 (model not loaded).

#### Schemas

See *POST /detect — multipart upload*, the first request of this endpoint.

item.name: POST /detect — JSON with an image URL (SSRF-checked)

request.description:
Fetch the image yourself-free: hand the detector a URL and it fetches it.

**The URL is SSRF-checked first** (`common.net.validate_url`). This container sits on `ai_shared`, so an unchecked URL input would be a request to proxy into the private network — anything resolving to an RFC1918, loopback, or link-local address is a **400**, and EVERY resolved address must clear the list, not just the first. A container-name or LAN URL will not work here on purpose; set the `imageUrl` collection variable to a public image.

Note `labels` here is a comma STRING rather than an array — both spellings are accepted in JSON as well as multipart.

**Errors:** 400 (blocked or unresolvable URL, bad scheme, undecodable image), 502 (the remote host failed the fetch or timed out — DETECTOR_FETCH_TIMEOUT, 20 s), 503 (model not loaded).

#### Schemas

See *POST /detect — multipart upload*, the first request of this endpoint.

Prometheus exposition for the HTTP surface (request counts, latency histograms, in-progress gauge), added by prometheus_fastapi_instrumentator — the same instrumentation the classifier uses.

Scraped by the `prometheus` container as the `detector` job (`ai/litellm/prometheus.yml`), so you normally read this in Prometheus rather than here; this request is for checking the endpoint is alive after a recreate.

**Returns** text/plain, not JSON.

#### Schemas

Response `200` (`text/plain`) — Prometheus text (prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator's HTTP metrics).

item.name: MCP
item.description:
The MCP surface, registered with LiteLLM as the `detector` server (`ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml` → `mcp_servers`). One tool: `detect_objects`.

These requests speak JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP to the service's own `/mcp` endpoint through the pass-through. A model reaching the tool through LiteLLM's MCP routing never builds these by hand — they are here for debugging the tool definition and its answers. LiteLLM does NOT execute tool calls for you; see ai/litellm/LITELLM_MCP.md for the orchestration loop.

MCP requires both `application/json` and `text/event-stream` in Accept.
